metadata.research_goal: Create a backend-ready basketball knowledge draft covering rule variants, court structure and zones, game phases, positions and modern hybrid roles, role-specific responsibilities, physical demands, injury/load risks, and beginner/intermediate/advanced role-development implications.
metadata.scope_note: Primary scope is 5v5 indoor basketball. Store competition_rule_set on production records because NBA, FIBA, NCAA, youth, and local leagues differ in court dimensions, timing, foul limits, timeout rules, goaltending details, and shot-clock resets.

key_concepts.title: Continuous invasion game with constrained possessions
key_concepts.summary: Basketball is played by two teams of five trying to score in the opponent's basket while preventing scores. The shot clock makes offensive possessions time-constrained and rewards quick advantage creation, shot quality, offensive rebounding, and transition defense preparation.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store possession state, clock pressure, and phase tags on drills and tactical records.

key_concepts.title: Rules require competition variants
key_concepts.summary: NBA, FIBA, NCAA, NFHS, youth, and local leagues differ in court dimensions, period length, foul limits, timeout rules, shot-clock operation, defensive restrictions, and substitution administration. Backend records must not assume one universal timing or foul model.
key_concepts.backend_use: Add competition_rule_set and rule_edition fields to all rule, court, timing, and foul records.

key_concepts.title: Position is a role, not only height
key_concepts.summary: Traditional labels map to point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, and center, but modern lineups blur roles through combo guards, wings, small-ball bigs, stretch bigs, and switchable defenders. Training should store offensive role, defensive matchup, and transition duty separately.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use role_profile plus phase_responsibility arrays instead of one static position description.

key_concepts.title: Court zones shape shot value and spacing
key_concepts.summary: The restricted area, paint, elbows, slots, wings, corners, short corner, dunker spot, post, and above-the-break areas carry different tactical value. Role profiles should specify where players create, finish, space, screen, rebound, and defend.
key_concepts.backend_use: Court-zone records should be linked to role tasks, shot profiles, and drill constraints.

key_concepts.title: Use offense, defense, transition, and special-situation phases
key_concepts.summary: Basketball demands change by settled offense, settled defense, offensive transition, defensive transition, and special situations such as baseline/sideline out-of-bounds, jump balls, free throws, late clock, end-game, and after-timeout actions.
key_concepts.backend_use: Normalize tactical content by phase and special situation before generating practice plans.

key_concepts.title: Basketball load is repeated multidirectional work plus contact
key_concepts.summary: Basketball requires repeated accelerations, decelerations, lateral shuffles, jumps, landings, pivots, screens, boxouts, and short recovery intervals. Guards often accumulate more high-speed and shuffling work, while bigs absorb more collision, wrestling, rebounding, and landing load.
key_concepts.backend_use: Tag role demands by acceleration, deceleration, lateral, jump_land, contact, and aerobic_repeatability components.

key_concepts.title: Lower-extremity risk dominates basketball
key_concepts.summary: Ankle sprains, knee injuries, patellar tendon symptoms, and overuse knee complaints are common basketball risks. Risk is amplified by landing traffic, rapid deceleration, cutting, fatigue, contact rebounding, and game intensity.
key_concepts.backend_use: Attach ankle, knee, tendon, landing, and load-monitoring warnings to basketball programs.

key_concepts.title: Development should progress from general skills to role constraints
key_concepts.summary: Youth and beginner training should build all-around ball handling, passing, shooting, footwork, spacing, defense, and decision-making before over-specializing. Advanced players need role-specific constraints, game-speed reads, small-sided games, and phase-specific decisions.
key_concepts.backend_use: Map beginner/intermediate/advanced progression onto role records while preserving all-around fundamentals.

entities.team_foul_penalty: Common fouls above four team fouls in a regulation period create penalty free throws; overtime has a lower quota.
entities.substitutions: Substitutes report to scorer, remain in substitution box area, and enter when beckoned at legal opportunities.

technical_models.backend_use: Default NBA rules profile for professional North American program templates.

entities.team_foul_penalty: Team fouls are tracked by quarter; after the team-foul limit, eligible defensive fouls produce free throws.
entities.substitutions: Five team members from each team are on court and may be substituted through substitution opportunities.

technical_models.backend_use: Default international rules profile for FIBA and many non-US competitions.

court_zones.definition: Team's own basket side of the court until the ball and player advance to frontcourt under the relevant rule set.
Opponent basket side of the court where half-court offense, spacing, screening, and defensive shell are organized.
Lane and near-rim space including restricted/no-charge area depending on rule set.
Free-throw-line extension and high-post decision area.
Top and slot perimeter areas above the break.
Perimeter areas between slots and corners.
Deep sideline-baseline spacing areas where the 3-point distance differs by rule set.
Baseline-adjacent finishing and post spaces below the block, short corner, and dunker spot.

technical_models.backend_use: Use zone IDs to constrain drills, shot profiles, spacing roles, and defensive rotation teaching.

phases.description: Half-court possession against an organized defense.
Organized half-court defense after the offense is set.
Attack immediately after rebound, steal, turnover, made basket, or long outlet before defense is fully set.
Recover and stop early offense after shot, turnover, or missed rebound.
Dead-ball, clock, and score situations requiring pre-planned execution.

technical_models.backend_use: All role profiles and tactical rules should reference phase IDs.

tactical_rules.principle: Maintain usable spacing before and after the first advantage so drives, rolls, cuts, and kick-outs do not crowd each other.
implementation_cues: occupy both corners when lineup permits
keep a dunker or short-corner option only when it improves rim pressure
replace on baseline cuts
lift or drift on paint touch
trail big spaces above break when shooting threat exists
role_dependencies: wings hold width then attack closeouts
bigs screen or space based on shooting and matchup

tactical_rules.principle: Create an advantage with pace, screen angle, mismatch, drive, post seal, or ball movement; convert it with rim shot, open three, free throw, offensive rebound, or continued advantage pass.
implementation_cues: do not over-dribble after help commits
pass to the next advantage
screen defender not grass
attack closeout foot and hip
recognize low-man rotation

tactical_rules.principle: Possessions should be taught with early, middle, and late clock decision rules because the shot clock changes shot quality thresholds and risk tolerance.
A stop is not complete until the defense secures the rebound or forces a dead-ball/turnover outcome.
implementation_cues: contain the ball without opening middle unnecessarily
tag rollers and recover
low man protects rim then finds body
all five communicate shot and boxout
guards crack back on long rebounds

tactical_rules.principle: The first three steps after change of possession decide spacing, rim protection, and matchup quality.
implementation_cues: rebounder outlets or pushes immediately
guards sprint wide or middle based on assignment
nearest defender stops ball
big protects rim before finding matchup
trail communicates cross-matches

tactical_rules.principle: Ball-screen and off-ball-screen coverage must define ball defender, screen defender, low man, tagger, and weakside closeout responsibilities.
role_dependencies: wings tag rollers and close out to shooters

tactical_rules.principle: Defensive aggression should adapt to personal fouls, team fouls, bonus state, time, score, and opponent free-throw quality.
implementation_cues: avoid unnecessary reach fouls in penalty
protect players near foul-out
teach verticality and legal guarding
distinguish tactical foul context by rule set
know late-game free-throw and timeout implications

physical_demands.summary: Basketball combines repeated high-intensity accelerations and decelerations, lateral shuffling, short sprints, jumps, landings, pivots, contact screens, boxouts, and intermittent aerobic recovery.
programming_implications: blend multidirectional speed with braking mechanics
train repeated efforts with incomplete recovery
include contact-tolerant trunk and hip strength

physical_demands.notes: Guards commonly perform more high-intensity shuffling and sprinting than forwards and centers, with frequent direction changes and defensive chase work.
Wings must combine guard-like perimeter movement with forward-like rebounding, contact finishing, and matchup versatility.

high_priority_demands: hip mobility for drops and switches
physical_demands.notes: Bigs may accumulate less open-court sprinting than guards but face high collision, screening, rebounding, vertical contest, and static wrestling demands.

higher_exposure_roles: bigs and wings in rebound traffic
guards and wings with high cutting load
bigs with repeated jumping and landing
female athletes require explicit ACL prevention emphasis

mitigation: manage spikes in minutes and plyometrics
alternate high and low neuromuscular days

avoid: teaching plays without defensive coverage context
conditioning that ignores deceleration and lateral demands
single-skill workouts detached from phase context

priorities: upper and lower body contact strength

transition_responsibilities: safety after deep drive or shot
beginner_development: learn defensive stance and ball pressure

defense_responsibilities: help from nail or low man when assigned

offense_responsibilities: space corner or slot if skilled

transition_responsibilities: protect rim first in defensive transition
fill wing when point guard pushes

defense_responsibilities: defend bigs while preserving spacing value
protect rim as secondary big when at four
